title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: S&P 500 slipped 0.15% to 7,707 in Tuesday's post-Labor Day session as megacap tech dragged (Apple -2.6%, Alphabet -2.1%, Microsoft -2.1%), while Caterpillar (+1.65%), Honeywell (+0.95%) and Home Depot (+0.88%) led gainers.

Markets: Oil holds near 6-week highs after last week's ~8-10% surge in WTI/Brent on renewed US-Iran strikes; Goldman Sachs warns crude could spike toward $120/barrel if shipping attacks escalate, though steady Strait of Hormuz throughput is capping the worst-case fears.

Macro/Policy: US-Iran conflict intensified over the weekend — US struck radar and mine-laying sites off Iran's coast, Iran retaliated with drone/missile attacks on US Mideast bases; national gas average hit $4.15/gal and diesel a record $5.85/gal.

Macro/Policy: Fed stays divided ahead of the Sept 15-16 meeting — hawkish dissenters (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) are pushing for a hike after last week's hot August jobs report (+162K vs +55K expected), with minutes signaling rate cuts may be off the table until 2027.
Companies: Casey's General Stores reports earnings today, kicking off a busy week with Chewy (9/9) and Oracle, Macy's and Adobe (9/10) still to come.
